report.source_text: CT of the facial region with contrast showed abnormal soft tissue thickening in the region of the right side of the face with thickening and enhancement of right lacrimal gland, mild pre-septal swelling, thickening and enhancement of temporalis, lateral pterygoid and muscles of mastication on the right side. These findings were likely representing infected/inflammatory process (figure 2). There was pansinusitis with air fluid levels in bilateral maxillary sinuses and sphenoid sinuses. Pneumatised petrous temporal bone apex was visualised with fluid within it. There were ill-defined hypodensities in bilateral cerebellar hemispheres and right temporal lobe. These findings indicated possibility of an infarction.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 67-year-old man with uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and ischemic heart disease was hospitalized for non-severe COVID-19 pneumonia. On day 3 of treatment, he developed acute right-sided rhinocerebral involvement with black eschar on the right cheek and hard palate, right eye swelling, and right eye ophthalmoplegia. CT imaging revealed pansinusitis with bilateral maxillary and sphenoid sinus involvement, soft tissue thickening and enhancement of right lacrimal gland, temporalis, lateral pterygoid, and muscles of mastication, and ill-defined hypodensities in bilateral cerebellar hemispheres and right temporal lobe consistent with angioinvasive disease and infarction. Histopathology of biopsy specimens from the right cheek skin, right eyeball, and nasal tissue demonstrated numerous aseptate fungal hyphae, confirming the diagnosis of mucormycosis. Emergency surgical intervention including right face debridement, right eye exenteration, and bilateral functional endoscopic sinus surgery was performed with ICU admission. Postoperative imaging confirmed interval removal of orbital structures and right cheek soft tissue with packing of defects, and maturation of cerebral infarcts in the right cerebellum, right hemipons, and right temporal lobe.
